- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 2–3 days after spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust downward by 1–2% for next 7–14 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if volatility > 2% over last 5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 10-day moving average), model tends to lag; forecast should align with 10-day MA by day +2.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction for next 3–5 days.
